description.narrative:
Kosovo Competitiveness Study will determine Kosovo’s most optimal path to competitiveness by examining the data (facts) and considering various developmental alternatives (scenarios).
The study will focus on involving all the relevant stakeholders to jointly develop and take ownership of an overarching competitiveness study that focuses on: a) Economy, b) Business Environment, and c) Education.
The aim is to draft a comprehensive competitiveness study with concrete developmental plans for improving conditions in the following sectors:
Economy - including standard of living, poverty eradication, employment, economic inclusiveness, anti-monopoly policies, trade competitiveness, openness to trade.
Business Environment - including entrepreneurial environment, business infrastructure, access to credit, investor protections, labour market flexibility.
Education - including access to education, quality of education, human capital.

The Management Development Associates Foundation (MDAF), a Kosovo-based Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) applied to Sida for funding of 2 million SEK to carry out the “Kosovo Competitiveness Study” post COVID-19 resilience, in Kosovo during the period 2020-2021. The intervention Kosovo Competitiveness Study aims to determine Kosovo’s most optimal path to competitiveness by examining the data (facts) and considering various developmental alternatives (scenarios). The study will focus on involving all the relevant stakeholders to jointly develop and take ownership of an overarching competitiveness study that focuses on: a) Economy, b) Business Environment, and c) Education. The aim is to draft a comprehensive competitiveness study with concrete developmental plans for improving conditions in the following sectors: Economy - including standard of living, poverty eradication, employment, economic inclusiveness, anti-monopoly policies, trade competitiveness, openness to trade. Business Environment - including entrepreneurial environment, business infrastructure, access to credit, investor protections, labour market flexibility. Education - including access to education, quality of education, human capital. The intervention’s total budget is 4 million SEK, out of which the organization’s own funding is approximately 2 million SEK (188,094 EURO) and the remaining approximately 2 million SEK (188,060 EURO) is contributed by Sida.

The main objective of the intervetion is a comprehensive competitiveness study with concrete developmental plans for improving conditions in the following thematic areas: economy, business environment and education.

The following results have been achieved: Result 1 Platform Development The www.kosova2040.com platform, for the first time, aggregated data from 14 public institutions and made them public. The platform played an important role serving as an input in the drafting process for the National Development Strategy by the Strategic Planning Office (SPO) under the Prime Ministers Office of Kosovo. During the seven (7) regional meetings, the overall feedback by the participants from the Public, Private and NGO sectors was that they would use the platform for their projects and activities to support their missions, be it lobbying or advocating for changes in policy level or perception. No subsequent study was done that can assess the platforms effectiveness; however, visits and usage numbers show high traffic using google analytics. Data-driven decision-making is the main selling point of the www.kosova2040.com platform. The platform can serve as the foundation for future policy making and further expanding public data for other dimensions necessary for the National Development Strategy and overall PPD in Kosovo. The SPO has already used the platform in their preparatory workshops for the NDS 2030. The Prime Ministers Office have shown interest to expand the platform to include additional data related to Health, Environment, Safety and Security, the rule of law, and Governance.
Result 2 COVID-19 Impact Assessment The Covid-19 impact assessment on Kosovos economy report was a one-time study that provided a snapshot of more than 1200 registered businesses in Kosovo. Tools developed and used for digital questionnaires distributed through SMS proved effective and cost less than traditional studies using face to-face surveys. Furthermore, the SMS driven survey was deemed necessary due to covid restrictions. The study itself was used to input the discussion and was distributed in all seven (7) regional PPD events.
Result 3 PPD Meetings The implementing partner MDAF organised meetings with representatives from the Public (central and local government), leading regional companies and NGOs. Furthermore, the presentations were tailored to each region, comparing the data from the respective regions vs the national level. According to a representative from the Office of the Prime minister Strategic Planning Office, data gathered from these regional meetings helped them elaborate the sectoral strategies, part of the National Development Strategy 2030. SPO representatives declared that the format used in the seven (7) regional meetings would be replicated in the future to gather data from the Private Sector continuously. There was an overall consensus between the public, private and NGO sectors in every regional PPD event, to escalate the frequency of the dialogue and work together to improve public and private education to reflect the real needs of the private sector and ensure higher education employability of youth. Private sector and NGO representatives asked that the government consult them when taking any measures that will affect the private sector, especially regarding Covid 19.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
